statement: For constant matrices \mathbf{A}, \mathbf{B}, \mathbf{C} and matrix variable \mathbf{X}, the derivative of the matrix quadratic trace function \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{AXBX^\top C}) with respect to \mathbf{X} is \frac{\partial \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{AXBX^\top C})}{\partial \mathbf{X}} = \mathbf{B^\top X^\top A^\top C^\top} + \mathbf{BX^\top CA} in numerator layout, and \frac{\partial \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{AXBX^\top C})}{\partial \mathbf{X}} = \mathbf{CAXB} + \mathbf{A^\top C^\top XB^\top} in denominator layout. (Note: the supplied source derives this matrix quadratic trace derivative; it does not contain a derivation for the vector quadratic form \mathbf{x}^\top \mathbf{A} \mathbf{x}.)

symbols.meaning: matrix variable with respect to which differentiation is performed
trace operator summing diagonal elements of a square matrix

steps.text: Apply cyclic permutation of the trace \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{ABCD}) = \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{DABC}) to cycle \mathbf{C} to the front and commute the differential operator with the trace: d\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{AXBX^\top C}) = d\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{CAXBX^\top}) = \operatorname{tr}(d(\mathbf{CAXBX^\top})).

Apply the product rule for matrix differentials to the product (\mathbf{CAX})(\mathbf{BX^\top}): \operatorname{tr}(d(\mathbf{CAXBX^\top})) = \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{CAX}d(\mathbf{BX^\top}) + d(\mathbf{CAX})\mathbf{BX^\top}).

Distribute the trace over the sum of differentials by linearity of trace: \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{CAX}d(\mathbf{BX^\top}) + d(\mathbf{CAX})\mathbf{BX^\top}) = \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{CAX}d(\mathbf{BX^\top})) + \operatorname{tr}(d(\mathbf{CAX})\mathbf{BX^\top}).

Evaluate differentials using constancy of \mathbf{A}, \mathbf{B}, \mathbf{C} and the transpose rule for differentials d(\mathbf{X^\top}) = (d\mathbf{X})^\top: \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{CAXB}d(\mathbf{X^\top})) + \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{CA}(d\mathbf{X})\mathbf{BX^\top}) = \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{CAXB}(d\mathbf{X})^\top) + \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{CA}(d\mathbf{X})\mathbf{BX^\top}).

Apply trace transpose invariance \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{M}) = \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{M^\top}) to the first term, where (\mathbf{CAXB}(d\mathbf{X})^\top)^\top = (d\mathbf{X})\mathbf{B^\top X^\top A^\top C^\top}: \operatorname{tr}(((\mathbf{CAXB}(d\mathbf{X})^\top))^\top) + \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{CA}(d\mathbf{X})\mathbf{BX^\top}) = \operatorname{tr}((d\mathbf{X})\mathbf{B^\top X^\top A^\top C^\top}) + \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{CA}(d\mathbf{X})\mathbf{BX^\top}).

Apply cyclic permutation of the trace \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{UV}) = \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{VU}) to move d\mathbf{X} to the right in both terms: \operatorname{tr}((d\mathbf{X})\mathbf{B^\top X^\top A^\top C^\top}) + \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{CA}(d\mathbf{X})\mathbf{BX^\top}) = \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{B^\top X^\top A^\top C^\top}(d\mathbf{X})) + \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{BX^\top CA}(d\mathbf{X})).

Factor out d\mathbf{X} and express the differential in both canonical forms using linearity and transpose: \operatorname{tr}((\mathbf{B^\top X^\top A^\top C^\top} + \mathbf{BX^\top CA})d\mathbf{X}) = \operatorname{tr}((\mathbf{CAXB} + \mathbf{A^\top C^\top XB^\top})^\top d\mathbf{X}).

Convert the differential form to derivative form: in numerator layout, \frac{\partial \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{AXBX^\top C})}{\partial \mathbf{X}} = \mathbf{B^\top X^\top A^\top C^\top} + \mathbf{BX^\top CA}; in denominator layout, \frac{\partial \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{AXBX^\top C})}{\partial \mathbf{X}} = \mathbf{CAXB} + \mathbf{A^\top C^\top XB^\top}.

assumptions.assumption: Matrices \mathbf{A}, \mathbf{B}, and \mathbf{C} are constant with respect to \mathbf{X}.
assumptions.breaks_when: Any of \mathbf{A}, \mathbf{B}, or \mathbf{C} is a function of \mathbf{X}, requiring additional differential product terms.

assumptions.assumption: Matrix dimensions are conformable such that \mathbf{AXBX^\top C} is well-defined and a square matrix.
assumptions.breaks_when: Inner matrix dimensions do not match for multiplication or the resulting product matrix is non-square, causing the trace operator to be undefined.

assumptions.assumption: A single layout convention (numerator layout vs denominator layout) is consistently maintained throughout.
assumptions.breaks_when: Formulas from numerator-layout and denominator-layout conventions are mixed without taking the transpose.

failure_modes.signature: Derivative expression appears transposed relative to expected layout (e.g. \mathbf{CAXB} + \mathbf{A^\top C^\top XB^\top} instead of \mathbf{B^\top X^\top A^\top C^\top} + \mathbf{BX^\top CA}).
failure_modes.cause: Confusing numerator-layout with denominator-layout definitions without verifying author conventions.

failure_modes.signature: Terms in the derivative appear in an invalid matrix product order.
failure_modes.cause: Assuming matrix multiplication commutes when applying the product rule or cyclic trace rearrangements.

failure_modes.mode: Direct application of scalar chain rule to scalar-by-matrix trace functions
failure_modes.signature: Invalid derivative expression failing to account for matrix dimensions or transpositions.
failure_modes.cause: Exact equivalents of the scalar chain rule and product rule do not apply directly to matrix-valued functions of matrices without differential forms.
